Description: Fetch role-access records matching a given HTTP method+path. Cache-first (Redis) then DB fallback with dynamic path matching. Called by every service's AccessGuard on every authenticated request.
Criticality Reason: Hot path — every authenticated request across the entire platform hits this endpoint. Failure = all services lose authorization checks, complete platform outage.
Important Log Fields: method, path, cache_hit, result_count, duration_ms, trace_id
Sensitive Data: JWT token in Authorization header, role names in response
Dependencies: DB: RoleAccess.findAll (Sequelize/MSSQL), Redis: cache get/set with key role:{method}:{path}, Access Management Service (self)
Existing Observability: SDK auto HTTP+Sequelize+Redis spans only. Active logging commented out. No custom metrics.
Observability Gap: No active logging (commented out). No custom metrics. No domain-level trace context. Cache hit/miss ratio invisible. No alerting on authorization failures.
Notes: Highest priority endpoint in the entire fleet. Must have latency histogram, cache hit ratio, and error rate metrics. Consider adding a dedicated health check for Redis availability since cache failure degrades this to DB-only and impacts all services.

Description: Paginated list of all role-access records with filtering by roleName/path/isAccessRemoved and ordering. Admin listing endpoint.
Criticality Reason: Admin-only listing. No business impact if temporarily unavailable. Used for role-access management UI, not on the critical auth path.
Existing Observability: SDK auto HTTP+Sequelize spans only. All logging commented out.
Notes: Low priority — admin read-only endpoint. Standard request logging sufficient.

Description: Bulk-grant a role access to multiple routes for a project. Checks for duplicates (409 CONFLICT), bulk-creates records, invalidates+sets Redis cache per route.
Criticality Reason: Grants access permissions in bulk. Incorrect grants could create unauthorized access. Used during project/role onboarding. Failure during onboarding blocks new role setup.
Important Log Fields: role_name, project_id, route_count, created_by_user_id, trace_id, conflicting_routes (on 409)
Sensitive Data: JWT token. user.id from decoded token stored as createdById.
Dependencies: DB: Route.findByPk (per routeId), RoleAccess.findOne (conflict check per route), RoleAccess.bulkCreate. Redis: cache del+set per method+path.
Existing Observability: SDK auto HTTP+Sequelize+Redis spans. All logging commented out.
Observability Gap: No active logging. No domain event. No audit trail. No metrics. Bulk operations with no observability — if a partial failure occurs mid-batch, no record of which routes succeeded.
Notes: Should emit access.bulk_permission_granted domain event with route_count and role details. Needs audit logging for compliance — who granted which permissions, when.

Description: Toggle isAccessRemoved boolean on a role-access record (grant↔revoke). Finds by PK, flips boolean, invalidates Redis cache. 404 if not found.
Criticality Reason: Directly controls whether a role can access a specific API route. Revoking access immediately blocks that role from the route on next request. Granting access opens a route. Security-critical toggle.
Important Log Fields: role_access_id, role_name, route_path, method, old_value (isAccessRemoved), new_value, toggled_by_user_id, trace_id
Dependencies: DB: RoleAccess.findByPk, RoleAccess.update. Redis: cache del.
Existing Observability: SDK auto HTTP+Sequelize+Redis spans. All logging commented out.
Observability Gap: No active logging. No domain event. No audit trail of permission changes. This is a security-sensitive operation with zero observability — permission grants/revokes are invisible.
Notes: Security-critical. Must emit domain event distinguishing grant vs revoke. Must have audit trail. The toggle pattern (flip boolean) means repeated calls flip-flop — worth logging the before/after state to detect accidental double-toggles.

Description: Despite being a GET endpoint, performs writes. Reads routes from request body (non-standard), diffs against existing routes in DB (cache-first), bulk-creates new ones. Returns created routes.
Criticality Reason: Registers new API routes into the access management system. Required for new endpoints to be grantable. Failure means new routes can't be permission-controlled, but existing routes continue working.
Sensitive Data: JWT token. user.id stored as createdById.
Dependencies: DB: Route.findAll (cache-first via Redis routes:all), Route.bulkCreate. Redis: get routes:all, del routes:all after create.
Observability Gap: Has Winston logging (active) but not structured. No domain event. No metrics. GET-with-write-body is a REST anti-pattern that may confuse HTTP caching/proxies.
Notes: REST anti-pattern: GET method that writes. Body on GET is non-standard and may be stripped by proxies. No DTO validation on body (typed as 'any'). Worth flagging to service owner for eventual method change to POST.
